umbrella.title: Epic: CSP data-movement pattern coverage for CV / LLM / JEPA models
umbrella.scope: Umbrella for the pattern-coverage program: build the complete set of CSP data-movement patterns needed to execute the operators of computer-vision, LLM, and JEPA models on the credit-based dataflow simulator. One epic per core operator (including key fused operators); each epic decomposes into five medium (estimate 5) sub-issues: T1 pattern design & envelope analysis, T2 ISA/executor capability closure, T3 envelope-aware schedule generator, T4 functional integration & oracle, T5 regression & characterization. Staged in six dependency-ordered waves; sub-issues are filed when their wave opens. Definition of done: every operator in the plan's inventory maps to a closed epic and the four model blocks of the model-validation epic run end-to-end green in CI.

epics.title: Epic: pattern infrastructure hardening (partitioned credits, envelopes everywhere)
epics.scope: Close the infrastructure gaps that every pattern epic builds on: wire PartitionedCreditPool into the executor (restoring the original v0.9 design's per-matrix credit partitioning, per the #67 provenance), extend the #67 resource envelope to all existing generators, warn on generation/execution envelope mismatch, fix #18 (non-matmul Kernel factories don't compile their op), and scaffold the machine-checkable operator-by-pattern coverage matrix that the model-validation epic will assert.

custom_subs.d: Restore the original design's per-matrix (A/B/C) credit partitioning in the executor credit pools - defense-in-depth so hand-written or third-party schedules cannot monopolize buffers regardless of ordering. See the provenance analysis in #67.
Extend the #67 Config envelope (l3_buffer_count/l2_bank_count + per_matrix_burst_share) and constructive residency bounds to all existing schedule generators, not just matmul.
When a schedule's generation envelope differs from the executor's configured credit pools, surface a warning (and a validation issue) instead of silently executing under different assumptions.
Kernel::create_* factories for non-matmul ops must actually compile their op into the DMProgram (structural gap tracked in #18).
Machine-checkable operator-by-pattern coverage table (data file + test) that pattern epics update as they land and the model-validation epic asserts green.

epics.title: Epic: gather/scatter CSP movement pattern (indirect addressing)
epics.scope: Index-driven, non-contiguous tile movement: functional DMA_LOAD_GATHER / DMA_STORE_SCATTER (currently annotation-only no-ops), index-tile handling, and gather-feed schedules. Unlocks embedding lookup, KV-cache reads, and JEPA context/target token masking.

epics.title: Epic: broadcast + two-operand aligned streaming patterns
epics.patterns: P5 broadcast, P6 two-operand aligned streaming
epics.scope: One-to-many tile broadcast (functional STR_BROADCAST_ROW/COL, currently no-ops) and rate-matched dual-stream movement for binary elementwise ops (functional VE_ELEMENTWISE), including the credit implications of two producers feeding one consumer. Unlocks bias application, residual add, SwiGLU gating, and RoPE table distribution.

epics.title: Epic: streaming/online reduction pattern
epics.scope: Single-pass online reductions (running max/sum/mean/variance) with the row tile resident while statistics accumulate, then in-place normalization - functional VE_REDUCE plus running-stat support in the value-producing compute path. Upgrades the existing multi-pass softmax/norm approach and is the enabling primitive for flash-style attention.

epics.title: Epic: in-flight layout transform pattern (transpose/reshape/patchify)
epics.scope: Layout changes performed during movement rather than as separate passes: BM_TRANSPOSE beyond the current B-matrix case, functional BM_RESHAPE, patchify (image to token tiles), and attention head split/merge. Unlocks ViT front-ends, im2col, and attention plumbing.

epics.title: Epic: GEMM family CSP movement pattern completion
epics.scope: Complete the dense GEMM pattern family beyond square matmul: batched GEMM, strongly rectangular aspect ratios (tall-skinny/short-fat, as in QKV projections and logits), and envelope-aware weight-stationary and input-stationary strategies alongside the existing output-stationary and interleaved ones.

epics.title: Epic: Conv2D family CSP movement patterns
epics.scope: The convolution family: harden the im2col+GEMM path, add the direct sliding-window pattern with halo/overlap reuse (an input tile multicast to the multiple output tiles it contributes to), and cover depthwise (no cross-channel reduction), pointwise (1x1 as GEMM), and grouped variants.
epics.operator: conv2d family (im2col, direct/halo, depthwise, pointwise, grouped)

epics.title: Epic: pooling & spatial reduction CSP movement patterns
epics.scope: Max/average pooling as strided sliding-window reductions and global average pooling as a full spatial streaming reduction, sharing the halo-reuse movement of the conv family and the online-reduction primitive.

epics.title: Epic: online softmax CSP movement pattern
epics.scope: Upgrade the existing 4-pass softmax generator to a single-pass online-softmax movement pattern (running max + rescaled running sum, row tiles resident), the standalone form of the primitive that flash attention fuses.

epics.title: Epic: LayerNorm/RMSNorm CSP movement patterns
epics.scope: Single-pass mean/variance (LayerNorm) and root-mean-square (RMSNorm) streaming normalization with broadcast scale/shift, plus BatchNorm inference folding into adjacent ops. RMSNorm is on the LLM critical path.

epics.title: Epic: fused epilogue CSP patterns (matmul+bias+activation, conv+BN+relu)
epics.scope: Epilogue fusion: bias broadcast and activation applied on the DRAIN path so the GEMM/conv intermediate never round-trips to DRAM. Absorbs #47 (fused-operator lowering: matmul epilogue) as this epic's generator/functional tasks; the #45/#48-50 batched-MLP sweep suite is the validation companion.

epics.title: Epic: fused FFN block CSP pattern (SwiGLU/GELU-MLP)
epics.scope: The transformer FFN block as one fused movement pattern: gate and up projections, elementwise gating (SiLU/GELU), and down projection with the intermediate activations kept on-chip between the chained GEMMs.

epics.title: Epic: attention CSP patterns (chained GEMMs -> flash-style fusion)
epics.scope: Attention in two stages: first the chained QK^T -> softmax -> PV pattern with explicit intermediates, then the flash-style fusion - Q tile resident, K/V tiles streamed, online softmax rescaling the accumulator so the score matrix never materializes off-chip. The flagship fused movement pattern. One extra sub-issue beyond the standard five: online-softmax accumulator integration.

epics.title: Epic: KV-cache CSP movement patterns (append, paged gather)
epics.scope: Autoregressive decode movement: streaming append of new K/V tiles to a growing region, windowed and paged gather for attention over the cache, and the decode-step pattern (batch-1 tall-skinny GEMMs against cached tiles). One extra sub-issue: paged cache layout design.

epics.title: Epic: RoPE & positional CSP patterns
epics.scope: Rotary position embedding as a movement pattern: cos/sin table broadcast plus pairwise-rotation elementwise applied on the feed path to Q/K tiles, and the general shape for positional signals injected during movement.

epics.title: Epic: embedding & logits CSP patterns
epics.scope: The model's entry and exit: token-id-driven embedding row gather, and the logits projection as a tall-skinny GEMM against a very wide weight matrix (vocabulary dimension) with streaming-friendly blocking.

epics.title: Epic: ViT/CNN spatial boundary CSP patterns (patchify, upsample, transposed conv)
epics.scope: Spatial boundary operators: patchify/unpatchify (image <-> token tiles), nearest/bilinear upsample as strided replication reads, and transposed convolution as scatter-accumulate over the halo pattern.

epics.title: Epic: JEPA masking CSP patterns (token gather/scatter)
epics.scope: The JEPA-distinctive movement: context/target token selection as mask-index-driven gather into dense compute tiles, positional re-injection for the predictor, and scatter of predictor outputs back to target positions for the embedding-space comparison.
epics.operator: JEPA context/target masking and predictor movement

epics.title: Epic: model-block validation (ResNet/ViT/Llama/I-JEPA through CSP)
epics.deps: all prior epics for the respective block
epics.scope: End-to-end validation: a ResNet block, a ViT encoder block, a Llama decoder block, and an I-JEPA block executed through the CSP executor with oracle-verified values under default and constrained envelopes, plus the CI-asserted pattern coverage matrix from the infrastructure epic. Definition of done for the whole program.

template_subs.d: Data-movement characterization for OPERATOR: reuse, residency, and working-set analysis; SURE/domain-flow derivation where applicable; envelope-derived block-size formula per the #67 constructive-safety discipline; design doc in docs/plans/.
Implement the annotation-only opcodes or executor capabilities OPERATOR needs, with functional semantics in the value-producing path (tile payloads / FunctionalComputeSpec machinery from #66).
Schedule generator + strategies for OPERATOR with constructive livelock-safety (per_matrix_burst_share), plus ScheduleValidator rules.
Value-producing execution of OPERATOR on the CSP executor, verified elementwise against a host reference oracle.

Execution regression for OPERATOR (strategy x size x envelope matrix, test_multi_tile_execution style), credit/stall invariants, and performance characterization (cycles, utilization, stall breakdown) recorded in the epic.

E12.d: Integrate the online-softmax running max/sum rescaling into the flash-attention accumulator path so the PV accumulation is correct under streamed K/V tiles.

E13.d: Design the paged KV-cache tile layout (page size vs tile size vs envelope) and its gather index scheme.
